questions.q: In 2016, a Florida man was charged with assault with a deadly weapon after throwing ____ through a Wendy's drive-thru window.
questions.note: Three and a half feet long. He said it was a prank. The gator was released unharmed.

questions.q: In 1945, a Colorado chicken named Mike survived without his head for ____.
questions.note: Fed with an eyedropper. Toured the country. Died in a motel in Phoenix.

questions.q: Fredric Baur, the man who designed the Pringles can, was buried ____.
questions.note: His kids stopped at Walgreens on the way to the funeral home. They went with Original.

questions.q: The Great Molasses Flood of 1919 killed ____ people in Boston's North End.
questions.note: A two-story wave of syrup moving 35 mph. Locals swear it still smells on hot days.

questions.q: Until 1948, 7 Up contained ____.
questions.note: Original name: Bib-Label Lithiated Lemon-Lime Soda. Really rolls off the tongue.

questions.q: Wisconsin man Don Gorske has eaten more than ____ Big Macs since 1972.
questions.note: He keeps the receipts in boxes. Guinness has verified it. His wife has not left.

questions.q: In 2007, an American woman named Erika held a commitment ceremony and 'married' ____.
questions.note: She took its last name. Before that she was in a serious relationship with her bow.

questions.q: A 1997 episode of Pokémon sent ____ Japanese children to the hospital.
questions.note: Flashing red-and-blue Pikachu attack. The episode has never aired again anywhere.

questions.q: In 2010, the millionaire owner of the Segway company died after ____.
questions.answer: riding a segway off a cliff
questions.note: Into a river. On his own estate. You could not write this.

questions.q: In 2006, an Australian man put ____ up for auction on eBay with a starting price of one cent.
questions.note: Bids reached $3,000 before eBay pulled it. New Zealand was not consulted.

questions.q: In 2009, a California woman sued PepsiCo because Cap'n Crunch's Crunch Berries ____.
questions.note: Dismissed. The judge ruled a reasonable consumer would know. Harsh but fair.

questions.q: In 2014, Red Bull paid $13 million to settle a class action lawsuit alleging that ____.
questions.answer: it does not actually give you wings
questions.note: Anyone who'd bought a can since 2002 could claim $10. Nobody grew wings.

questions.q: In 2018, a Florida man was arrested after trying to pay for his McDonald's order with ____.
questions.note: At the drive-thru. The employee declined. He left without food.

questions.q: Iowa farmer Charles Osborne had the hiccups nonstop for ____.
questions.note: 1922 to 1990. An estimated 430 million hiccups. They stopped a year before he died.

questions.q: In 1567, the mayor of Braunau, Austria died after tripping over ____.
questions.note: Four and a half feet long. He usually kept it rolled up in a pouch. Not that day.

questions.q: Astronomer Tycho Brahe kept a pet moose that died after ____.
questions.answer: getting drunk and falling down the stairs
questions.note: At a party. It drank too much beer. Tycho also had a metal nose. Different story.

questions.q: In 2017, a Florida woman was charged with DUI while riding ____ down a highway.
questions.note: Blood alcohol twice the legal limit. The horse was charged with nothing.

questions.q: In 2007, a New Jersey judge tossed a drunk-driving charge because the man was driving ____, which legally isn't a motor vehicle.
questions.note: Top speed in the single digits. Can't leave the rink. Case closed.

questions.q: In 2014, a California woman had to be rescued by firefighters after getting stuck in ____ of a man she'd met online.
questions.note: Six dates in. He'd ended it. They had to take the chimney apart to get her out.

questions.q: The 1814 London Beer Flood killed ____ people when a brewery vat burst.
questions.note: A 15-foot wave of porter. The brewery was found not liable. Ruled an act of God.

questions.q: In 2015, a Colorado Springs man got fed up with his computer, carried it into an alley and ____.
questions.note: Months of blue screens. He got a ticket for discharging a firearm. Said he felt better.

questions.q: Turkish construction worker Ilker Yilmaz holds the world record for squirting milk out of his eye a distance of ____.
questions.note: Snorted it up his nose first. Set in 2004. The record still stands, somehow.

questions.q: In 2015, Nicolas Cage agreed to hand over a $276,000 item he'd bought at auction after learning it was stolen: ____.
questions.note: Tyrannosaurus bataar, smuggled out of Mongolia. He outbid Leonardo DiCaprio for it.

questions.q: Keith Richards once told a magazine that he had snorted ____.
questions.note: Mixed with cocaine, he said. Then he said he was joking. Then he said he wasn't.

questions.q: On his 20th birthday in 1970, Bill Murray was arrested at Chicago O'Hare for ____.
questions.answer: trying to fly with 10 pounds of weed
questions.note: He'd joked to another passenger that he had bombs in his bag. They searched it.

questions.q: In 1961, Alan Shepard became the first American in space and spent the flight ____.
questions.note: Four-hour launch delay. Fifteen-minute flight. Nobody had planned for a bathroom.

questions.q: In 2002, 72-year-old Buzz Aldrin ____ a man who called him a coward and a liar.
questions.note: Right hook, outside a Beverly Hills hotel. No charges filed.

questions.q: Before Sally Ride's week-long shuttle flight, NASA engineers asked her if ____ tampons would be enough.
questions.note: Her answer: 'No. That would not be the right number.'

questions.q: In 2009, a Florida woman called 911 three times because McDonald's ____.
questions.note: She'd already paid. They offered a McDouble. She called it an emergency.

questions.q: In 2017, a Florida man called the sheriff's office to report that someone had stolen ____ from his car.
questions.note: Deputies found more in his pocket. Arrested on the spot. Case solved, sort of.

questions.q: Australian Graham Barker holds the Guinness record for the world's largest collection of ____.
questions.note: Harvested nightly since 1984. Stored in jars. Mostly one color.

questions.q: A male honeybee dies immediately after mating because ____.
questions.note: With an audible pop. The queen then moves on to the next one. And the next.

questions.q: The Argentine lake duck has the longest penis of any bird, measuring up to ____.
questions.answer: 17 inches, the length of its body
questions.note: Corkscrew-shaped. The duck itself is about 17 inches long. Do the math.

questions.q: Nearly every turkey sold in American supermarkets was conceived by ____.
questions.note: Bred so top-heavy they physically can't do it themselves. Somebody has that job.

questions.q: During Prohibition, the US government killed an estimated ____ people by deliberately poisoning industrial alcohol.
questions.note: To discourage drinking. Bootleggers stole it anyway. People kept drinking.

questions.q: The Guinness Book of Records was created in the 1950s to ____.
questions.note: The Guinness boss lost a bar argument about the fastest game bird. So he made a book.

questions.q: In the 1890s, Pope Leo XIII awarded a Vatican gold medal to ____.
questions.note: Vin Mariani. He reportedly carried a flask of it. Thomas Edison was also a fan.

questions.q: During World War II, the German army issued its soldiers tens of millions of tablets of ____.
questions.note: Brand name Pervitin. Also sold in chocolates marketed to housewives.

questions.q: In 2011, firefighters in Sweden had to rescue a moose that got stuck in a tree after ____.
questions.note: It was climbing for more apples. After the rescue it slept it off on the lawn.

questions.q: In 1970, Oregon highway officials tried to dispose of a dead eight-ton whale using ____.
questions.note: Blubber came down a quarter mile away and crushed a car. Most of the whale stayed put.

questions.q: The world's shortest scheduled airline flight, in Scotland's Orkney Islands, covers ____.
questions.note: Scheduled at 90 seconds. The record is 53. There is no beverage service.

questions.q: The chainsaw was invented in the 1780s to help with ____.
questions.note: For cutting through the pelvis when the baby got stuck. Hand-cranked. You're welcome.

questions.q: In 1932, Pittsburgh millionaire Eben Byers died after drinking roughly ____ bottles of radium-laced 'energy' water.
questions.note: His jaw fell off. He's buried in a lead-lined coffin.

questions.q: In 2012, thieves in the Czech Republic made off with ____.
questions.note: They showed up with fake paperwork saying it was being demolished. Sold it for scrap.

questions.q: In 1923, jockey Frank Hayes won his first and only race while ____.
questions.note: Heart attack mid-race. The horse, Sweet Kiss, finished first anyway. Buried in his silks.

questions.q: The winner of the 1904 Olympic marathon was kept on his feet by trainers feeding him ____.
questions.note: Rat poison, booze, and raw egg whites. He was hallucinating. He got the gold.

questions.q: In 1970, Pirates pitcher Dock Ellis threw a no-hitter while ____.
questions.note: He thought it was his day off. Walked eight. Could only see the catcher's glove.

questions.q: In 2014, an Orlando man was arrested after witnesses saw him ____ at Lake Eola Park.
questions.note: Also kicked a sleeping duck. Charged with animal cruelty. The swans are fine.

questions.q: In 2007, Texan Jackie Bibby set a world record by sitting in a bathtub with ____ live rattlesnakes.
questions.note: He wore shorts. He holds a separate record for rattlesnakes held in his mouth.

questions.q: In 1962, three schools in Tanganyika had to close because of an epidemic of ____.
questions.note: Started with three girls. Spread for 18 months. Nobody was having a good time.

questions.q: French entertainer Michel Lotito, known as Mr. Eat-Everything, spent two years eating ____.
questions.note: Also bikes, shopping carts and a coffin. Guinness gave him a brass plaque. He ate it.

questions.q: In the 1950s and 60s, the CIA paid sex workers in San Francisco to lure men to a safehouse so agents could ____.
questions.note: Operation Midnight Climax. Agents watched through a two-way mirror, drinking martinis.

questions.q: In the 1960s, the CIA spent years and millions of dollars trying to turn ____ into listening devices.
questions.note: Microphone in the ear, antenna in the tail. Project abandoned. The cats did not care.

questions.q: In 1975, a physics paper in a respected journal listed ____ as a co-author.
questions.note: F.D.C. Willard. The author had written 'we' throughout and didn't want to retype it.

questions.q: Mozart wrote a six-part canon in B-flat major titled ____.
questions.note: K. 231. There's a follow-up in the catalog: 'Lick My Ass Nice and Clean.' Genius.

questions.q: In 2012, Wisconsin police arrested a man on drug charges whose legal name was ____.
questions.note: Changed from Jeffrey Wilschke in 2011. Arrested again in 2013 and 2017. Same name.

questions.q: Since 1961, a city ordinance in Gainesville, Georgia has made it illegal to eat fried chicken with ____.
questions.note: Gainesville calls itself the poultry capital of the world. Still on the books.

questions.q: The tiny town of Rabbit Hash, Kentucky has repeatedly elected ____ as its mayor.
questions.note: Recent mayors include a pit bull, a border collie, and a French bulldog named Wilbur.

questions.q: In 1989, the Soviet Union paid Pepsi for soda syrup with ____ submarines and three warships.
questions.note: Briefly made Pepsi one of the largest navies on Earth. They sold it all for scrap.

questions.q: In 1986, Cleveland tried to set a world record by releasing ____ balloons at once.
questions.note: They came right back down. Shut an airport, a highway, and a Coast Guard rescue.
